subtopics.title: Push and Pull: The Engine of Rural–Urban Migration

questions.question: Which of the following is a PUSH factor in rural–urban migration?
options: A cousin offering a bed in Gauteng

questions.question: The phrase "real or believed" attached to pull factors matters because:
options: Push factors are stronger than pull factors
Migrants often move on the perception of opportunity, which the city may not deliver
Cities always deliver what they promise

questions.question: Rural–urban migration in South Africa is selective, meaning it mainly involves:
Rural depopulation is best defined as:
options: The decline of the population living in rural areas
The growth of villages into towns
The building of new rural clinics

questions.question: The closure of a rural school or bank branch feeds depopulation because:
options: Each closed service removes a reason to stay, pushing more families out in a downward spiral

questions.question: The population structure left behind by sustained out-migration is best described as:
options: Hollowed out — children and the elderly remain while the working-age middle is missing

questions.question: A balanced evaluation of out-migration notes that it also brings:
options: Guaranteed urban jobs for all migrants
Remittances sent home and eased pressure on overworked communal land

subtopics.title: Strategies, Social Justice and Access to Resources

questions.question: The logic test for any anti-depopulation strategy is whether it:
Agri-processing plants in rural areas fight depopulation by:
options: Reducing the number of clinics needed
Creating work where people live, adding value to local produce

questions.question: The Natives Land Act of 1913 is central to rural social justice issues because it:
options: Confined black land ownership to a small fraction of South Africa

questions.question: Depopulation runs hardest in former homeland districts partly because these areas:
options: Concentrated large populations on the least productive land with little infrastructure investment

questions.question: Land tenure reform is distinctive because it:
options: Strengthens the rights of people already on the land without moving anyone
Returns land taken in forced removals

questions.question: Land redistribution differs from restitution because redistribution:
options: Requires proof of a specific historical removal
Is forward-looking — it transfers farmland for equity and livelihoods without a specific historical claim
Only protects farm dwellers from eviction
Applies only to land inside national parks

questions.question: A restitution claim must relate to dispossession that happened:
options: After 19 June 1913, under racially discriminatory laws

questions.question: Successful land reform acts as a depopulation strategy because:
options: It forces people to move to cities
Secure rights and productive land offer a rural livelihood without migrating

questions.question: In the kitchen-table picture, the plot that is too small to split again for the next generation is:
Migration happens, in the shove-and-tug picture, when:
options: The shove and the tug together beat the comfort of staying home

questions.question: "The city promises more than it pays" reminds us that many migrants:
options: Arrive to unemployment and informal settlements despite the believed promise

subtopics.title: The Village After the Taxi Leaves

questions.question: The "pinched-waist" population pyramid of a depopulating village shows:
options: Children and pensioners present but the working-age middle missing

questions.question: New brick rooms rising beside old homesteads in a depopulating village are visible evidence of:
options: Remittances sent home by urban workers

questions.question: The "slow leak" comparison describes depopulation as:
options: A seasonal cycle that reverses each year
A gradual, self-feeding decline as leavers trigger service closures and more leaving

questions.question: Which strategy correctly matches its target push factor?
options: Electrifying the village — aimed at thin services
Closing the clinic — aimed at unemployment
Raising taxi fares — aimed at drought
Mechanising farms — aimed at creating jobs

subtopics.title: Three Repairs for One Old Injustice

questions.question: The family that has worked a farm for generations but can be evicted next month needs which repair?
options: Tenure reform — a stronger grip on land they already occupy

questions.question: The three-verb summary of land reform is:
The only land reform leg that looks backwards at one specific, named removal is:
Land reform closes the loop with migration because a family with secure, productive land:
options: Has a living at home, removing the need for the one-way taxi
Is required to lodge a land claim
